steps.description: Fit one PyDESeq2 negative-binomial model with design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment on the 16 samples after a minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=4 samples, the smallest group size). Median-of-ratios size factors are estimated inside the model; counts are used as delivered with no length offset. Set reference levels explicitly (WT, vehicle) and report them. Run three Wald results: (1) the genotype:treatment interaction coefficient — the drug-effect difference KO vs WT, the primary answer; (2) the simple drug effect in the reference genotype WT (treatment coefficient); (3) the simple drug effect in KO (treatment + interaction contrast). Apply apeglm-style LFC shrinkage (pydeseq2's native implementation, coef-based) to the single coefficients, report unshrunken log2FC and lfcSE alongside for every result including the composite KO contrast (pydeseq2 does not support shrinkage on arbitrary contrasts). Keep Cook's-distance outlier flagging on (p-value set to NA in a cell with <7 replicates) and report the count of NA genes separately. Adjust p-values with BH at alpha 0.05 within each contrast with independent filtering kept on, pass alpha=0.05 to the results step, and inspect the p-value histogram before trusting the adjusted values.

plan.title: Drug×genotype interaction DE in heart, PyDESeq2
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is whether the drug's effect differs between KO and WT hearts. That is the genotype:treatment interaction of the 2x2 factorial in counts.csv (12,000 genes, 16 samples, 4 replicates per cell), so the plan fits one negative-binomial GLM with both factors and their interaction term in PyDESeq2 (Python per user constraint), tests the interaction coefficient by Wald test, and reports the two simple effects (drug effect in WT, drug effect in KO) beside it. Steps follow the grounded procedure: sample-structure QC on blind VST before any test, a minimal pre-filter with median-of-ratios normalization inside the model, BH at alpha 0.05 within each contrast, and a report that names reference levels and carries fit diagnostics. Count provenance is Salmon as delivered with no length data, so the model runs on counts as delivered with no length offset, stated in the report. No reference gene sets are needed; no enrichment step is planned because the research question does not ask for pathways.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.
